app.title: DyingStar - Dev panel
msg.dockerUnreachable: the engine still does not answer
msg.intercepted: the cluster's game server traffic comes to port {port}
msg.serverDied: the Godot server stopped (see its tab)
msg.serverFrozen: PID {pid} is FROZEN: it listens but uses no CPU any more — restart it
msg.stackComingBack: the stack is installed, its pods are coming back…
msg.waitingPods: already started, waiting for the pods…
net.hostsMissing: {n} name(s) missing from the hosts file
net.noCluster: the cluster cannot be read yet
net.ok: {n} relays up, names in the hosts file
net.tunnelMode: tunnel mode: the network is the start-dev script's business
probe.hzNoDoor: horizon is ready in the cluster but has no way in: neither WebTransport (no UDP NodePort on the service, or on Windows the {relay} relay is stopped), nor Traefik (127.0.0.1:80: the tunnel or its relay is down), nor the expose-horizon relay ({port}).
probe.hzNoEndpoint: horizon has no ready endpoint: even if a door listens, nothing is behind it.
probe.serverFrozen: PID {pid} is FROZEN (0 CPU) — it listens but no longer runs
probe.staleForward: 127.0.0.1:{port} listens but the tunnel is STALE: opened {age} min before the oldest horizon pod still alive, so it points at a pod that is gone. The client will fail to connect. Fix: the "Horizon relay" button (it frees the port first).
quit.detail:
"Stop everything" stops the Godot server, the clients and the relays.
The cluster is not concerned: its deployments and databases stay as they are.

"Leave them running" quits the panel but abandons these processes: they keep
going with no interface to see them or stop them.
quit.title: Quit the dev panel
setup.allDone: Everything is in place. Close this screen and use "Start everything".
setup.godot.fetch: Downloaded from the project's releases (about 110 MB), checked, unpacked next to the sources.
setup.godot.help: The project uses its own build of the Godot editor (C#, double precision). The one from godotengine.org does not work with it.
setup.godot.nupkgsHelp: They come with that Godot build.
setup.godot.title: Godot
setup.logHint: The output of each step is in the "setup" log tab.
setup.repo.big: Not cloned yet. Large: about {size} MB, several minutes. Goes to {folder}.
setup.repo.small: Not cloned yet (about {size} MB), goes to {folder}.
setup.repos.help: The project's repositories, cloned into the workspace folder. A folder that already exists is never touched: no update, no branch change.
setup.repos.title: Sources
setup.stack.help: Everything the game needs behind it, running in the local cluster: about thirty services. The first start downloads their images and takes 10 to 25 minutes; the following ones take a couple of minutes.
setup.stack.name: Services
setup.stack.start: Runs the repository's start-dev script without the tunnel: no administrator rights needed. By hand: ./scripts_linux/start-dev.sh --no-tunnel (Windows: .\scripts_windows\start-dev.ps1 -NoTunnel).
setup.stack.title: The local stack
setup.subtitle: What this machine still needs to run the project
setup.sys.winget: Installed through Windows' own package manager (winget). Windows will ask for permission.
setup.sys.wingetRestart: Installed through Windows' own package manager (winget). Windows will ask for permission, and you will have to sign out and back in before Docker works.
setup.title: Setup
setup.tool.fetch: The panel downloads version {version} from its publisher, checks it, and keeps it in its own folder. No administrator rights, nothing else on the machine is changed.
setup.tool.ok: Already on this machine, nothing to do.
setup.tools.help: What the project runs on. git fetches the sources, Docker runs the containers, minikube is the small local cluster, kubectl talks to it, Helm installs things in it, and the .NET SDK builds the C# part of the game.
setup.tools.title: Programs
setup.ws.help: One folder for the whole project: the repositories and Godot go in it, side by side. Pick an empty folder on a disk with room (about 10 GB), or the folder where you already cloned things.
setup.ws.title: Workspace folder
tp.mismatch: client {client} does not match the cluster's traffic manager {manager}: install the same version
tp.notInstalled: Telepresence is not installed (or not on your PATH)
ui.build.hint: Every service runs the published image by default. Building a target compiles it inside minikube's docker and repoints its Deployment at it, with no commit at all: the Applications' ignoreDifferences keep ArgoCD from undoing it. This is how you test your own changes, horizon-data included: it carries the props definitions, and without rebuilding it horizon ignores a local definition silently. ⚠ godotserver takes several minutes.
ui.build.tip: Builds {name} from {path} inside minikube's docker, then repoints the {deployment} Deployment at it.
ui.build.title: Build an image
ui.chain.title: Start sequence
ui.clear.tip: Clear the log on screen (the .log files are kept)
ui.clearOnRestart.tip: Each time a process restarts, its log starts from scratch: the tab only shows the last run. The .log files keep everything.
ui.danger.deleteHint: ⚠ Deleting the cluster erases minikube and everything in it: the databases, so the players and the objects of the world. Everything will have to be installed again (10 to 25 minutes).
ui.danger.purgeHint: ⚠ Purging deletes the persisted objects of the world. ArgoCD undoes within seconds a horizon scaled to zero (selfHeal): the purge would then run under a live horizon, which writes everything back at once. Suspend selfHeal before purging.
ui.danger.title: Red zone
ui.deleteCluster.tip: The clean-dev script of the kubernetes repository: minikube delete. Irreversible.
ui.detailHint: Click a line to read it in full here.
ui.filter.tip: Only shows the lines that match.
ui.folder.tip: Open the folder of the .log files
ui.game.title: Editor and clients
ui.gate.delete: Docker does not answer: nothing to delete.
ui.gate.hostsOk: The hosts file is already right.
ui.gate.netTunnel: Tunnel mode: nothing to do here.
ui.gate.notOurs: The panel can only stop or restart a server it started itself: one started with F5 in the editor does not belong to it and must be closed in the editor.
ui.gate.purge: The k8s stack is not ready: ScyllaDB cannot be reached.
ui.gate.relay: The k8s stack is not ready: nothing to relay.
ui.gate.relinkFrozen: The game server is FROZEN: restarting horizon would be useless, restart the server first.
ui.gate.relinkNeeds: It takes the k8s stack ready AND a server listening on {port}: without both, restarting horizon cannot bring a link back.
ui.gate.serverUp: A server already listens on {port}. Use "Restart the server".
ui.highlight.tip: Shows everything and highlights the matches.
ui.need.horizon: Horizon cannot be reached: a client could not connect.
ui.need.link: Horizon is not linked to the game server: you would spawn unable to move. Wait a moment, or restart horizon.
ui.need.server: No game server is listening: you would spawn with nothing to make you move.
ui.need.serverAlive: The game server is FROZEN (it listens but uses no CPU any more): you would spawn unable to move. Restart it.
ui.need.world: The world was not delivered to the game server: you would spawn without your spawn parent, so unable to move. Restart horizon.
ui.net.hint: How this machine reaches the cluster without minikube tunnel: the stack's names point at 127.0.0.1 in the hosts file (written once, with permission), and three small relay containers forward to the cluster. They restart with Docker: no console to keep open. Repair puts the relays back in line with the cluster, for example after it was recreated. To use the tunnel of the repository's scripts instead, change "Network path" in the settings.
ui.net.title: Network
ui.npc.hint: Deployed by ArgoCD (service-npc): it runs by itself. Its log is in the service-npc tab.
ui.npc.restart.tip: Deletes its pod: Kubernetes recreates it. One restart, nothing else in the stack is touched.
ui.npc.title: NPC service
ui.on.clients.tip: Clients are already running; this button adds more.
ui.on.editor.tip: The Godot editor is already open; clicking will do nothing.
ui.on.server.tip: A server already listens on {port}; clicking will do nothing.
ui.on.stack.tip: start-dev is already running; stop it first to run it again.
ui.platform.hint: ArgoCD reconciles the cluster by itself: once installed, the stack comes back on its own each time minikube starts. This button runs the repository's start-dev script, which creates the cluster when there is none and installs ArgoCD in it.
ui.platform.title: Platform
ui.pods.delete: Delete the pod (it will be recreated)
ui.procs.none: No process started by the panel.
ui.procs.title: Processes
ui.purge.tip: TRUNCATE on the objects table: deletes the persisted objects of the world.
ui.regex.tip: Read the search as a regular expression.
ui.relay.tip: The expose-horizon script of the repository: a relay that FOLLOWS the horizon pod and restarts itself when the pod changes. It is also the only way in from another machine of the network.
ui.relink.tip: Recreates the horizon pod. Horizon finds the game server again by itself, so this is only for when the link does not come back. It deletes the pod rather than "rollout restart": the latter edits the Deployment, ArgoCD reverts the edit, and horizon restarts TWICE.
ui.server.killGhosts.tip: Kills headless Godot processes left behind by a closed editor. What the panel started is spared.
ui.server.restart.tip: Stops the dedicated server, waits for the port to be free, then starts it again. Use it to pick up a change in the server code.
ui.server.stop.tip: Stops the dedicated server without starting it again. Use it to free memory when it grows.
ui.server.title: Game server
ui.stack.start.tip: The start-dev script of the kubernetes repository: minikube, ArgoCD, Traefik, the tunnel and the hosts entries. It needs elevated rights for the tunnel and the hosts file.
ui.stale: The panel was updated: close it and start it again to finish the update. Until then some texts and buttons may be missing.
ui.tp.hint: The documented way to run the game server from your sources. Connect gives this machine the cluster's names and routes (Windows asks for permission). Intercept then sends the traffic meant for the cluster's game server to your local one. The output of each command is in the telepresence tab. The panel quits Telepresence before it starts minikube: restarting minikube while connected breaks name resolution in the cluster.
ui.tp.title: Telepresence
